title: What Is the Best Organic Fertilizer for Pechay?
metaTitle: Organic Fertilizer for Pechay: Compost, Manure and FAA
metaDescription: Organic fertilizer for pechay: how much compost and aged chicken manure to use, how to make FAA and FPJ at home, and a simple plan from bed to harvest.
excerpt: The best organic fertilizer for pechay is mature compost or fully decomposed chicken manure, worked into the bed before planting. Add a weekly fish amino acid (FAA) spray while the leaves grow. Pechay is ready 3 to 4 weeks after transplanting, so its nitrogen must already be in the soil. Homemade liquids help, but they cannot replace a rich bed. anee.io, a farm app built for Filipino farmers, dates every feeding from your own planting day.

blocks.text:
Pechay, or petsay, is one of the quickest crops on a Filipino farm. The ATI Central Visayas guide harvests it 3 to 4 weeks after transplanting. A DA Cordillera organic guide harvests it about 35 days after planting. So it has no time to wait for slow fertilizer.

That is the catch with organic fertilizer for pechay. Compost and manure release nitrogen slowly, as soil life breaks them down. So build a rich bed before planting, then top up with quick liquid feeds.

items: **Base:** 2 to 4 kg of mature compost per square meter of bed, the rate in the DA Cordillera organic vegetable guide.
**Chicken manure:** only fully decomposed, never raw, because pechay is eaten fresh and harvested within weeks.
**Vermicast:** a strong choice for leafy growth, mixed into the bed with the compost.
**Liquid top up:** fish amino acid sprayed weekly while the leaves grow.
**Honest limit:** homemade liquids are supplements, not a full meal.

blocks.text: Which organic fertilizer for pechay works best?
Use a solid base plus a quick top up. Here is how the common choices compare.

blocks.text: The VSU study, in the Annals of Tropical Research, compared swine manure, chicken dung, mudpress and vermicast for pechay. All of them raised nitrogen release and pechay growth. But the swine manure it tested carried high levels of lead, nickel, copper and zinc. Later, a 2025 trial under VSU conditions found vermicast stood out for leaf growth and fresh weight.
How much compost and manure does pechay need?

The DA Cordillera organic vegetable guide applies 2 to 4 kg of compost per square meter as the base. A common 1 by 20 meter bed is 20 square meters, so it takes 40 to 80 kg. The guide allows only fully decomposed compost manure, and never manure from dogs, cats or people.

For chicken manure, the ATI Central Visayas guide puts one sack on each 20 meter bed, mixed in or covered with soil. But its program also adds 1 kg of 14 14 14 and 4 kg of urea per bed. A strictly organic bed leaves those out, so it needs the higher compost rate.
Why chicken manure must be aged

Iowa State University Extension says raw manure should go on at least 120 days before you harvest vegetables that touch the soil. Leafy vegetables carry the greatest risk. Since pechay is harvested about five weeks after planting, raw manure cannot meet that gap.

Composting fixes this. A pile that reaches 55 degrees Celsius kills many weed seeds and germs. It also cuts the ammonium that makes fresh poultry manure burn roots. But composting lowers the nitrogen the crop can use right away, so top up with liquids.
How do I make homemade fertilizer for pechay?
Two homemade liquids from ATI Cordillera suit pechay, and worms can make a third input. Our list of [organic fertilizer examples](/blog/organic-fertilizer-examples) covers more.
Fish amino acid (FAA)

Chop 1 kg of fish with its bones, gills and guts. Mix it with 1 kg of molasses or muscovado in a covered clay jar, kept in the shade. After 10 to 15 days, pour off the liquid into bottles, leaving a third of each bottle empty. ATI Cordillera sprays 2 tablespoons per liter of water every 7 days, from newly planted seedlings onward.

The University of Hawaii also calls FAA a nitrogen source for the leafy stage and sprays leafy vegetables weekly. But it dilutes it far more, at 1 part to 1,000 parts water. It also warns that spraying in full sun can burn the leaves.
Fermented plant juice (FPJ)

Chop 1 kg of young shoots, such as kangkong, kamote tops or alugbati, and mix in 1 kg of muscovado. Ferment for 7 to 10 days in a cool, dark place, then strain. ATI Cordillera sprays 2 tablespoons per liter every 3 to 7 days, before sunrise or late in the day. Think of FPJ as a tonic, not a main nitrogen source.
Vermicast

Build a shaded bed of rice hull or sawdust, then add chopped crop residues and animal manure. Release about 1 kg of worms per square meter and keep it moist but not wet. ATI Cordillera harvests the vermicast 30 to 45 days later, when black granules show on top.

blocks.title: Two guides, two strengths
blocks.text: ATI Cordillera mixes FAA at 2 tablespoons per liter, while the University of Hawaii uses 1 part in 1,000. If you are new to it, try the weaker mix on a few plants first. Spray only in the cool of the morning or late afternoon.
A simple organic feeding plan for one pechay bed

items.title: Build the bed
items.text: Mix 40 to 80 kg of mature compost into a 1 by 20 meter bed. Fully decomposed chicken manure and vermicast can share the load.

items.title: Raise strong seedlings
items.text: Sow in trays or a seedbed and spray FAA weekly at the mild rate once the seedlings are up.

items.title: Transplant at 2 to 3 weeks
items.text: Set the seedlings 10 cm apart in rows 20 cm apart, as the ATI guide does. Water right after and then daily.

items.title: Top up every week
items.text: Spray FAA once a week while the leaves grow, with FPJ in between if you have it.

items.title: Harvest at 3 to 4 weeks
items.text: Harvest early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Then compost the leftovers for the next bed.

blocks.text: Is organic fertilizer for vegetables enough on its own?

It can be, if the bed is rich. If organic pechay stays pale and slow, add more mature compost to the next bed and keep up the weekly FAA. If you do not sell as certified organic, you can also mix the two, as the ATI program does. Our guide to [organic vs inorganic fertilizer](/blog/organic-vs-inorganic-fertilizer) weighs both. For fruiting crops, see [fertilizer for vegetables](/blog/fertilizer-for-vegetables-philippines).

The same compost and FAA also work as organic fertilizer for plants in pots. For the planting steps in Tagalog, read [pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).
How does anee.io help with an organic pechay plan?

Pechay runs on short cycles, so it suits a new bed every week or two. In anee.io, write the plan once in the [Protocol Builder](/features/protocol-builder): compost on bed day, then FAA every 7 days. blocks.text: Questions about organic fertilizer for pechay

items.q: Can I use fresh chicken manure on pechay?
items.a: No. Iowa State University Extension says raw manure should go on at least 120 days before harvesting vegetables that touch the soil. Pechay is ready in about five weeks, and fresh poultry manure can burn roots. Compost it first.

items.q: How often should I spray FAA on pechay?
items.a: Once a week while the leaves grow. ATI Cordillera uses 2 tablespoons per liter of water, but the University of Hawaii uses a much weaker 1 to 1,000 mix. Spray in the cool of the day.

items.q: How much compost does pechay need per square meter?
items.a: The DA Cordillera organic guide uses 2 to 4 kg of compost per square meter as the base. That comes to 40 to 80 kg for a bed 1 meter wide and 20 meters long.

items.q: Is vermicast better than chicken manure for pechay?
items.a: Each has its strength. A VSU study found chicken dung the richest in phosphorus, potassium and calcium of four organic amendments. A later pechay trial found vermicast best for leaf growth and fresh weight, so many growers use both.

items.q: What is the best homemade fertilizer for pechay?
items.a: Your own compost or vermicast as the base, plus FAA as the weekly top up. FPJ is a tonic for vigor, not a main feed.
